critique: Temporal decay of detection benchmarks with class-dependent rates (artifacts vs natural kinds) is a lovely hypothesis with a clean prediction; classification has some temporal-drift work but detection does not. Year-stamped annotation is the cost center.
reason: Fresh temporal-validity question with a falsifiable class-structure prediction.

critique: Inpainting head-class anchors to measure tail-class context dependency is a cleaner causal instrument than compositing, though inpainting artifacts are a confound needing matched-region controls, which the design includes. Standalone it's a finding; merged with 0263 it's a paper.
reason: Merge with 0263 as the second instrument in a tail-context-dependency study.

critique: Bias propagation from CLIP filtering into downstream detector weaknesses is a causal chain claim that data-curation papers gesture at but haven't traced end-to-end; related classification-side evidence exists on CLIP-filter effects. The three-way correlation design (filter rate, CLIP zero-shot, downstream AP) is the right instrument.
reason: High-significance curation-bias tracing; timely as CLIP filtering is ubiquitous.

critique: The cost-of-clean-data question matters for policy, but matching aggregate AP between license-clean and web-trained models to isolate domain absences is a fragile matching exercise with many confounds (architecture, scale, recipe). Hard to make causal.
reason: Confounded comparison; policy-relevant but not cleanly answerable with public artifacts.

critique: The averaging-axis convention (instance-pooled vs image-averaged AP) is an evaluation degree of freedom nobody audits, and the ranking-change hypothesis on dense datasets is instantly testable from cached predictions. Pairs naturally with the other metric-convention audits in this batch.
reason: Protected: cheap-to-falsify metric-convention audit with ranking stakes.

critique: Benchmarks oversampling object-rich frames relative to deployment streams is a real distribution mismatch, and empty-scene false-positive behavior is where detectors genuinely differ. Estimating deployment difficulty distributions defensibly is the soft spot.
reason: Deployment-relevant evaluation audit; empty-frame FP behavior is under-measured.

critique: Generator-stereotype import into tail classes via generative augmentation is a sharp typicality-split test of a practice that's rapidly becoming standard. Typicality annotation is subjective but a small adjudicated protocol suffices.
reason: Timely audit of generative tail augmentation with a falsifiable split design.

critique: Occlusion-flag error auditing is sound hygiene but the downstream stake (occlusion-stratified AP comparisons) is a niche use case. Low ceiling even if flags are noisy.
reason: Narrow stakes; fold into a broader annotation-quality audit if needed.

critique: Counterfactual clothing/background edits for person subcategories extends known spurious-correlation methodology to a detection setting with fairness overtones. Related counterfactual-fairness image editing exists in classification, so the detection-specific instantiation carries the novelty.
reason: Focus on safety-critical subcategories (e.g., police/medic identification) where the spurious-feature stake is concrete.

critique: Whether AP-rare gains are concentrated in a few easy tail classes is the single cheapest audit of the long-tail progress narrative, pure re-analysis of cached predictions. The median-tail-class statistic is the kind of number that gets quoted for years.
reason: Protected: cheap-to-falsify; potentially narrative-changing for the long-tail subfield.

critique: End-to-end tracing of one bias axis from pretraining statistics through feature probes to detection errors is the mechanistic study the bias literature lacks; each link is measurable but making the chain quantitative (mediation-style) is ambitious. High risk of dying in instrumentation.
reason: Protected: high-risk high-reward mechanistic bias tracing.

critique: Budget-matched re-benchmarking of long-tail methods is rigorous but needs eight full training runs and careful budget accounting whose conventions reviewers will contest. The cheaper re-analysis audits (0255, 0256, 0276) extract most of the same narrative value first.
reason: Defer training; run only if the re-analysis audits leave the budget question open.

critique: Exposure-based rarity for open-vocab detectors is the right definition and the leaderboard-reordering hypothesis is testable by counting captions plus re-stratifying existing evaluations. Overlaps conceptually with 0001's exposure regression, so they should be one paper, not two.
reason: Anchor of the exposure-vs-rarity thread; merge with 0001 at proposal time.

critique: The thing-stuff taxonomy critique is philosophically interesting but the proposed interaction-query evaluation is vague and the matched-compute pipeline comparison has too many free choices. Panoptic literature already motivates joint representations.
reason: Vague instrument; panoptic literature already carries the core argument.

critique: Compute-normalized frontiers for detection would be a landmark meta-science result, but re-training 8 methods at 3 budgets is the most expensive proposal in the batch and prior compute-matters critiques exist in classification/NLP. The one-seed design also undercuts its own rigor message.
reason: Shrink to 4 methods x 2 budgets x 2 seeds, or piggyback on 0283/0285's runs; the full grid is not fundable from this batch.

critique: Cross-framework variance of the same nominal method is a confound everyone suspects and nobody has quantified for detection; eighteen short runs is a fair price for a number the field will cite defensively forever. Clean design, near-certain informative outcome.
reason: Foundational reproducibility constant; either magnitude is a citable result.

critique: Stale-baseline decay directly attacks the field's progress narrative and has precedent in metric-learning and recommender-systems reality checks, which both proves the genre and erodes first-mover novelty. The 'papers' own tuning budget applied honestly' protocol is the differentiating craft.
reason: High-ROI flagship; prior-work attack found the genre exists but not the detection instantiation.

critique: A seed-variance lookup table across task regimes is the missing power-analysis standard for detection; classification has partial answers (e.g., Picard's torch.manual_seed(3407) and Bouthillier et al.) but no detection-specific variance-components study. Many short runs, but each is small by design.
reason: Standards-setting artifact; converts a vague norm into a lookup rule.

critique: Tuning-budget asymmetry as the engine of SOTA is the sharpest of the rigor family; the genre exists in ML broadly (Lipton & Steinhardt's troubling trends, 'tuned baselines' studies in NLP/recsys) but no one has run the budget-transfer experiment on detection papers. Selection of the 6 papers must be pre-registered to dodge cherry-picking accusations.
reason: High-ROI flagship with a pre-registrable, bounded design.

critique: Adaptive-overfitting forensics on test-dev exists for classification (Recht et al. line) and the detection version depends on assembling enough published val/test pairs, which may simply not be reported often enough. Data availability is the fatal risk, not the analysis.
reason: Feasibility-gate first: census how many papers report both val and test-dev before committing.

critique: Ablation sign-flip rates under reseeding is a devastatingly simple attack on component-level conclusions and nobody has done it systematically for detection. Thirty rows x 3 seeds is real compute but each row is a short run by construction.
reason: Protected: reviewer-disagreement-prone rigor bomb with bounded scope.

critique: Environment-stack sensitivity is documented anecdotally and in some reproducibility studies; a nine-run detection-specific audit is publishable only as a workshop note unless the effect is shockingly large. Subsumed by 0290's broader determinism audit.
reason: Low ceiling; covered by the determinism audit.

critique: PIL-vs-OpenCV decode/resize divergence hitting AP-small is a concrete, mostly-inference audit of an unreported hyperparameter, and the interpolation-kernel literature (e.g., antialiasing flags) suggests the effect is real. Best bundled with 0290/0288 into one 'silent variables' paper.
reason: Bundle with 0290 into a single silent-variables reproducibility study.

critique: A determinism audit across popular repos with source attribution (data pipeline vs kernels) is practical, bounded, and produces immediately actionable findings for maintainers. The attribution toggling design is what elevates it above anecdote.
reason: Actionable infrastructure audit; natural host for 0288/0289 as sections.

critique: Reporting-practice censuses exist in ML (e.g., reproducibility checklists studies) but the 'with teeth' re-experiment link—showing unreported fields correlate with irreproducibility—is the novel and important part. 300-paper coding is a grind but parallelizable.
reason: The correlational teeth distinguish it from checkbox censuses; D&B material.

critique: A matched-compute factorial audit of canonical detection tricks is the detection analogue of 'bag of tricks' studies but run adversarially; nobody has published the null results. Twenty short runs is honest money for a table the community would pin to the wall.
reason: High-value canonical-wisdom audit; expected nulls are the product.

critique: Latency-measurement inconsistency is widely suspected and partially documented (e.g., TensorRT-vs-PyTorch discrepancies in YOLO papers); the standardized-harness re-ranking with convention attribution is useful engineering science. MLPerf-style precedent caps novelty.
reason: Position as a convention-attribution study, not a benchmark launch; MLPerf inference exists.

critique: Checkpoint-selection inflation is a known sin without a detection-specific magnitude estimate; the dense-checkpointing instrumented design yields a correction table meta-analyses could actually use. Modest but certain payoff.
reason: Cheap, certain, and produces a reusable correction constant.

critique: The BN-vs-accumulation discrepancy is mechanistically understood (batch statistics differ by construction) and documented in framework issues and some papers; the clean attribution experiment is confirmatory rather than discovering. Workshop-scale.
reason: Mechanism already understood; confirmation has low ceiling.

critique: Pretrained-checkpoint provenance as a hidden variable overlapping method deltas is a quietly important audit; timm-era checkpoint proliferation makes it timely and ten short runs is a fair cost. Some transfer-learning papers touch this but none frame provenance as a confound of record for detection.
reason: Timely hidden-variable audit; bundles naturally with the silent-variables family.

critique: Adaptive-overfitting-to-validation quantification replicates a known classification-side literature (Recht/Roelofs line, Ludwig-Schmidt work) in detection; the per-query tax framing is nice but the intellectual move is imported wholesale. Detection-specific numbers have modest marginal value.
reason: Direct port of established classification-side findings; low novelty confidence.

critique: A hash-audit of circulating benchmark file variants is a genuinely original forensic angle; if materially different COCO/VOC copies exist in the wild and shift AP comparably to published deltas, that's a scandal-grade finding at near-zero compute. Risk is the boring outcome (all copies identical).
reason: Protected: cheap-to-falsify forensic long-shot with scandal upside.

critique: The composition test (do published gains stack?) has precedent in optimizer/NLP-augmentation studies but not for detection tricks; interference structure is the real scientific content beyond the headline. Implementation burden of 8 tricks in one codebase is the main cost.
reason: High-leverage stacking audit; interference matrix is the durable contribution.

critique: A reproduction-gap meta-analysis harvesting existing model zoos and reproducibility-challenge records is clever data reuse, and the 'missing fields predict gap size' regression gives it explanatory power beyond a mean. Ten targeted new reproductions anchor the causal reading.
reason: Meta-analytic capstone for the rigor family; mostly data collection.

critique: Energy accounting including NAS costs was prominently litigated for NLP (Strubell et al.) and Green AI followups; the detection-specific break-even framing adds little, and reconstructing energy from disclosures is guesswork-heavy. The numbers would be too soft to support the strong claim.
reason: Established genre, soft data; low marginal insight.

critique: Minimum-detectable-effect tables per benchmark, cross-referenced against 100 papers' claimed deltas, is the single most weaponizable rigor artifact in the batch and is pure bootstrap re-analysis. The claims-survey pairing turns a statistics exercise into a field indictment.
reason: Protected: cheap-to-falsify, standards-setting; anchor of the rigor family.

critique: A tuning-induced generalization tax measured via COCO-matched pairs on unseen datasets is a provocative inference-only test of the simplicity dividend, but disclosed search budgets are unreliable and pair matching invites confounds. High interpretive risk, high payoff if the correlation is clean.
reason: Protected: high-risk high-reward, inference-only; confound-control is the craft.

critique: Code release vs config completeness as predictors of reproduction gap redirects a policy debate with an observational-plus-reproduction design; 20 reproductions is real work but the regression is what venues need to set requirements. Complements 0300 closely enough to share infrastructure.
reason: Merge with 0300; same reproduction harness, one stronger paper.

critique: Random search as the null hypothesis for component gains replicates the NAS random-baseline reckoning (Li & Talwalkar; Yang et al.) in detection component design, which both validates the move and means Reviewer 2 will cite it as done. The detection design-space instantiation and 'search vs insight' quantification retain force.
reason: Strong null-hypothesis audit; must position against NAS random-search literature explicitly.

critique: Conformal-coverage breakage by NMS is a precise, original theoretical-empirical question; conformal detection papers exist (post-NMS calibration) but none treat suppression itself as the coverage-destroying step. Analysis-only on cached candidates makes it nearly free.
reason: Protected: cheap-to-falsify with genuine formal novelty; top-decile idea.

critique: Causal-fidelity benchmarks for attribution exist in classification (ROAD, deletion metrics) and some detection XAI work; the inpainting-intervention grid for detection with a trivial-baseline comparison is a solid but not surprising extension. The 'near-trivial-baseline' hypothesis is the punch.
reason: Lead with the trivial-baseline indictment of detection XAI, not the benchmark.

critique: Machine psychophysics with adaptive staircases imports a mature experimental science into detector evaluation; psychophysics-inspired CNN studies exist for classification (Geirhos line) but staircase-measured detection thresholds with deployment-prediction validation would be new. The threshold-predicts-failures claim is the ambitious part.
reason: Protected: methodological transplant with high originality; inference-scale cost.

critique: IRT on detection outcome matrices is the strongest efficiency-audit idea in the batch: IRT-for-ML-benchmarks exists (Martinez-Plumed et al.; NLP leaderboard IRT) so novelty rests on the detection instantiation, misfit-item audit, and short-test construction. Pure cached-prediction analysis with a certain informative outcome.
reason: Flagship analysis-only idea; prior IRT-benchmark work must be cited and differentiated.

critique: Design-based survey sampling for deployment-valid AP estimates brings real statistics into benchmark construction; the annotation budget and defining a defensible target population are the constraints. The systematic-difference hypothesis against convenience benchmarks is likely true and worth measuring.
reason: Methodologically serious D&B contribution; annotation-bounded.

critique: A GUM-style combined uncertainty budget for COCO AP composes components this batch measures separately (annotation noise, bootstrap, framework variance, nondeterminism) into one metrology-grade statement; no one has done this composition for any CV benchmark. It is the natural umbrella paper for the rigor family.
reason: Umbrella synthesis with standards-body gravitas; mostly composition of existing measurements.

critique: Sequential optimal design for ablations validated by replaying published grids as oracles is a clean simulation study with immediate practical value; Bayesian optimization literature is adjacent but nobody has packaged it as ablation-protocol guidance. Pure simulation on existing numbers.
reason: Cheap, useful, certain-outcome methodology transfer.

critique: EVT for rare detection failures is intellectually attractive but the validation loop (oracle-ish committee scoring on unlabeled streams, held-out rare events) is fragile and severity needs a defensible scalar. The statistical machinery may outrun the measurable ground truth.
reason: Anchor severity in a domain with real incident labels (e.g., driving datasets) or defer.

critique: Information-gain-per-view ranking for active perception is a coherent alternative metric but the controlled multi-view simulation is a niche construction whose conclusions may not travel. Active-vision community is small; impact ceiling is limited.
reason: Niche audience, heavy simulation scaffolding, uncertain transfer.

critique: Cost-sensitive evaluation reversing AP-based choices is well-trodden conceptually (cost curves, utility-based eval in classification); the closed-form reversal boundary and detection archetypes are modest additions. Useful engineering note, weak main-track bid.
reason: Fold the actuarial layer into 0255's frequency-weighted utility audit as its deployment-cost extension.

critique: Bandit-style annotation allocation across classes is adjacent to a large active-learning literature that already covers class-aware acquisition; the per-class-quota framing is a repackaging more than a new question. Simulation is cheap but the delta over AL baselines will be contested.
reason: Active-learning adjacency too strong; low novelty confidence.

critique: Slice discovery exists (Domino, spotlight methods) mostly for classification; program-synthesized interpretable predicates over detection metadata with human validation is a real extension though the synthesis machinery could balloon. The known-failure-recovery validation design is right.
reason: Position against Domino-style slice discovery explicitly; detection-specific predicates (density, size strata, co-occurrence) are the novelty.

critique: Human-AI complementarity routing is an active HCI/ML literature (learning-to-defer, rejection learning) and the detection instantiation with simulated humans is a straightforward port. The miscalibration-concentration claim is the only fresh wrinkle.
reason: Learning-to-defer literature covers the core; simulation-only humans weaken the claim.

critique: Weak-to-strong generalization is a hot alignment-adjacent topic (Burns et al. for LLMs) with almost no dense-prediction instantiation, and the controlled-error-structure design converts it into a real causal experiment. Risk is that the identifiable-conditions theory is hard to nail beyond correlational patterns.
reason: Protected: high-risk high-reward; timely transplant with a controlled design.

critique: Data Shapley and its truncated approximations are established (Ghorbani & Zou onward), including coarse-granularity variants; shard-level detection valuation is an application, not a question. The scale-transfer claim is the only novel scientific content and it needs many training runs.
reason: Established method applied sideways; compute-heavy for the marginal claim.

critique: Behavioral churn under AP-matched updates is documented in classification (regression in ML systems, backward-compatibility papers by Bansal, Srivastava et al.), so the measurement half is a port; the contract-suite-with-flip-budgets mechanism for detection is the genuinely new half. Industrially resonant.
reason: Strong applied-science bid; must cite backward-compatibility literature and lead with contracts.

critique: Case-control epidemiology on detection logs with controlled re-test validation is a genuinely fresh methodological import; the constraint is finding public video streams with dense enough failure metadata to build honest cohorts. The replication loop distinguishes it from error-analysis-as-usual.
reason: Feasibility-gate on data: pick the benchmark first, then commit.

critique: Queueing-aware frame dropping is a systems-conference topic (video analytics literature has content-aware frame selection) and detection-aware drop policies exist in that community. CV-venue fit is poor and the systems venues have adjacent work.
reason: Wrong venue for this portfolio; systems literature adjacency too strong.

critique: The uncertainty-visualization user study is real HCI science but 30-participant studies belong at CHI, not CVPR, and the effect will hinge on task design choices reviewers can't audit. Valuable but outside this portfolio's venue targets.
reason: Venue mismatch; HCI methodology outside batch competency.

critique: Likelihood-ratio evidence reporting is the forensic-science gold standard (speaker recognition, fingerprints) and porting calibrated LR frameworks to detection outputs is original for CV; the single-scenario validation keeps it honest and cheap. Natural companion to the plate-SR forensic idea (0238).
reason: Merge with 0238 into one forensic-standards-for-CV paper; LR framework is the spine.

critique: The 'half the residual errors are ground-truth problems' claim has direct precedent (Borji's COCO error diagnosis, missing-annotation studies, TIDE) so the number itself may be less shocking than hoped, but a rigorous two-annotator adjudication at deployment thresholds on a SOTA model is still the citable version. Cheap, decisive, high-reuse.
reason: Anchor annotation-quality claim; prior work erodes surprise, not value.

critique: The 2015-architecture-2026-recipe experiment is the cleanest possible attribution of a decade of detection progress, with partial precedent (ResNet strikes back for classification; modernized-baseline studies) that proves the genre works and will demand careful differentiation. A few training runs buy a field-level number.
reason: High-ROI flagship; classification precedent raises confidence the effect is large.

critique: Benchmark-subset selection for cheap ranking exists in NLP (tinyBenchmarks, IRT-based subsets) and classification, so the detection instantiation must lean on the stratification design and the 0.95 rank-correlation validation across 30 checkpoints. Pure re-analysis; merges naturally with 0309's IRT machinery.
reason: Cheap and useful; should be the applied half of the IRT paper (0309).

critique: The vestigial-RPN hypothesis is a beautiful minimal experiment (two training runs) with a real chance of a counter-intuitive result; anchor-free and DETR literatures imply proposals are dispensable, which both motivates and slightly scoops the question. Sparse R-CNN and dense-prior work must be engaged.
reason: Protected: simple counter-intuitive; two runs to a quotable finding.

critique: Augmentation-as-data-equivalents with a stable exchange rate is a genuinely deep question with partial classification-side precedent (augmentation vs dataset size studies); the exact-exchange-rate framing and cross-scale stability claim are the new content. The grid is expensive but each cell is small.
reason: Deep equivalence question; strongest of the training-science trio after 0327.

critique: Oracle-substitution decomposition of localization vs classification error has direct precedent (Hoiem et al. diagnostics, TIDE, Borji's analyses all decompose error types), so the headline is likely already known in essence. The modern-architecture refresh with a strong 'classification is the bottleneck' framing retains some value but not first-mover credit.
reason: Survives only as the framing device inside a broader modern-error-decomposition refresh; cite TIDE/Hoiem prominently.

critique: The cropping test bounding global-context value is a beautifully simple falsification of architecture-trend rhetoric; context-in-detection studies exist (classic context papers, out-of-context benchmarks) but none bound context value with a crop protocol on modern detectors. Cheap and quotable either way.
reason: Protected: simple counter-intuitive with a clean bound; inference only.

critique: Silhouette evaluation flips the texture-vs-shape literature (Geirhos) onto detection with GT-mask rendering as a cheap instrument; shape-bias work exists for classification so the detection port must emphasize the layout-preserved design and per-class structure. Either outcome revises the texture-primacy narrative for detection.
reason: Cheap falsification with an existing literature to collide with productively.

critique: The NMS-free-wins-are-tuning-artifacts hypothesis is a sharp adversarial-baseline attack on the DETR-era narrative, and post-processing tuning is inference-scale. DETR papers themselves report NMS ablations, so the attack must cover their exact configurations to stick.
reason: Protected: reviewer-disagreement-prone adversarial audit at inference cost.

critique: Scale-subsumption of label-assignment research is a plausible and important claim about a large literature (ATSS, OTA, SimOTA era), testable with six runs. The two-scale-points design is thin for a 'stops mattering' universal, but as an existence proof it works.
reason: Tests whether a whole subfield's deltas survive modern scale; bounded compute.

critique: Early-performance-predicts-final-ranking is well-studied in NAS and hyperparameter optimization (learning-curve extrapolation, successive halving); the detection-specific 0.9 correlation number is useful but the intellectual territory is claimed. Correlation likely degrades exactly on the interesting configs.
reason: Learning-curve-prediction literature owns this; detection number is incremental.

critique: Random-box pretraining touching full-supervision curves would be surprising, but the hypothesis as stated is probably false in the strong form and the weak form (heads warm-start cheaply) is unremarkable. Related to free-anchor/weak-supervision literature without a crisp differentiator.
reason: Strong form implausible, weak form uninteresting.

critique: Locating the size floor where human re-annotation agreement equals model-GT agreement makes small-object progress claims below that floor unfalsifiable — an epistemically foundational result at small annotation cost. Human-vs-model agreement curves by size have not been published for detection.
reason: Protected: cheap-to-falsify, foundational; among the best of the whole batch.

critique: The rank-invariance catalog (which pipeline stages use confidence magnitudes vs ranks) is a neat formal-empirical audit that reframes the calibration literature's relevance to detection pipelines. Pure analysis; the fusion/tracking breakage cases are where the value concentrates.
reason: Cheap invariance audit that reframes what calibration buys in detection.
